symptom: (7) LVS mismatch: missing, shorted, or open nets

first_checks.check: Examine the LVS summary report's text/label comparison section and unmatched net count.
first_checks.why_first: cheapest (takes seconds) and immediately separates systemic pin/text naming mismatches from physical layout shorts/opens

first_checks.check: Run the LVS layout short-isolation / short-finder utility in interactive layout viewer (e.g., Calibre RVE Short Finder).
first_checks.why_first: rules out the vast majority of physical shorts by tracing polygons to the exact intersection node

first_checks.check: Verify global power/ground port connectivity and implicit connection rules (e.g., VDD/VSS text/global declarations vs pin shapes).
first_checks.why_first: rules out catastrophic multi-thousand-net cascade failures caused by a single unattached power grid label

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Run short isolation with top-level text labels disabled vs enabled.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: If short disappears or changes node when text is disabled, the short is a false short caused by duplicate/misplaced text labels attaching to different nets.
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: If short persists identically on polygon connectivity alone, the cause is a genuine physical layout metal bridge or via bridge.

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Flatten the local macro/block boundary in extraction vs running hierarchical LVS.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: If short/open disappears in flattened run, the issue is a hierarchical port-alignment mismatch or boundary pin extraction bug.
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: If short/open persists in flat extraction, the physical connectivity inside the cell or routed layer is genuinely broken.

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Trace open net using virtual connect rules (disable VIRTUAL CONNECT COLON / CONNECT statements in LVS rule deck).
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: If open net count spikes drastically, the layout relies on implicit virtual connections that were missing physical stitching vias.
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: If open net count remains unchanged, the open is an explicit physical break in a continuous physical wire track.

common_root_causes.cause: Text/label pin name mismatch or floating pin text placed on the wrong metal layer or off-grid.
Missing fill/via or illegal metal line bridge introduced during automatic filler insertion / ECO routing.
Power grid / substrate tie-off missing or mismatched global VDD/VSS net names across IP block boundaries.
LVS deck layer derivation bug on complex multi-patterned or guard-ring layers.

classic_trap: Chasing thousands of individual signal shorts/opens reported by the tool when the actual single root cause is a missing power grid label that caused the tool to merge all power nets together.
node_era_note: At 7nm and below, coloring/multi-patterning (LELE/EUV) layer derivations and cut-layer via rules introduce false shorts in layout extraction that do not exist in simple single-exposure metal decks.

symptom: (8) LVS mismatch: wrong device sizes or extra devices

first_checks.check: Inspect the detailed device mismatch section of the LVS report to check if width (W), length (L), or fin-count (NF) is systematically scaled by a fixed factor.
first_checks.why_first: cheapest and immediately identifies grid-unit/scale factor misconfigurations or parallel device combining settings

first_checks.check: Check for dummy device or guard-ring transistor extraction in macro white spaces.
first_checks.why_first: rules out extra un-instantiated physical layout devices added for density/reliability (fillers/dummies) that lack schematic representation

first_checks.check: Verify parameter tolerance settings (e.g., LVS REDUCE / LVS TOLS) in the LVS rule deck.
first_checks.why_first: rules out false device size errors caused by tiny off-grid snapping or rounding differences in extraction

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Toggle LVS parallel/series device reduction settings (e.g., LVS REDUCE PARALLEL MOS) in the runset.
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: If extra devices disappear and size mismatch vanishes, the schematic uses multi-finger/parallel instantiations that the layout extraction failed to combine due to asymmetric source/drain connections or resistor insertions.
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: If extra devices remain, the physical layout contains actual extra poly/diffusion geometry touching active layers.

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Run LVS with dummy cell filter rules enabled vs disabled (e.g., LVS FILTER UNUSED MOS/RES).
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: If extra devices disappear, the extra devices are intentional floating fill/dummy transistors that need proper schematic dummy tagging or extraction filter rules.
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: If extra devices persist, the extra devices are functional transistors misplaced or erroneously drawn in active circuits.

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Compare extracted parameter delta against layout geometry (measure poly width/length directly in GDS/OASIS viewer vs schematic property).
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: If measured layout poly matches schematic but LVS reports a discrepancy, the LVS deck layer derivation (e.g., gate enclosure by active layer or STI stress layer rules) calculated an incorrect effective W/L.
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: If layout geometry physically differs from schematic, the PCell generation or sizing script injected the wrong parameter value.

common_root_causes.cause: Multi-finger or parallel device reduction failure due to un-merged source/drain nodes or subtle routing parasitic asymmetry.
Unfiltered dummy/fill transistors or decoupling caps present in layout but absent in schematic netlist.
Schematic vs layout parameter property unit mismatch (e.g., microns vs meters, or Fin count vs total width).
Poly / active layer enclosure overlap rule misinterpretation during LVS device seed layer recognition.

classic_trap: Manually resizing layout transistors to fix a reported size mismatch when the real issue is an extraction setting failing to recognize parallel fingers as a single reduced transistor.
node_era_note: At 28nm, planar transistor device size mismatch is continuous (W/L ratios); at 7nm and below (FinFET/GAA), transistor sizing is strictly quantized by integer Fin counts (NFIN), turning W/L mismatches into discrete Fin count or gate-pitch alignment mismatches.
